newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks power to new highs, set record close.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks power to new highs, set record close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rallied to a new record close on Tuesday, chiefly on momentum buying in index heavyweights HSBC Holdings Plc and Hongkong Telecom, but brokers warned many key stocks lagged the rally.
"It is chiefly momentum buying in HSBC ahead of its interim results," said Peter Lai, in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities. "Only a few stocks were really active."
The Hang Seng Index ended 116.30 points, or 0.76 percent, higher at a new record close of 15,487.24 after leaping to an all-time high of 15,508.96 in mid-afternoon.
Both of Tuesday's records eclipse those set on Monday.
Turnover was a robust HK$20.99 billion, higher than Monday's HK$19.07 billion but much lower than the record of HK$26.6 billion set on June 20.
"I don't think that we are seeing inflows of hot money from other Asia markets," said Lui. "We may be seeing some portfolio adjustments by institutions as well as the retail sector."
HSBC hit a new high of HK$255.00 then eased to close HK$5.00 higher at HK$254.00 on heavy turnover of HK$808 million.
HSBC will report its results for the first half of 1997 on August 4.
Hongkong Telecom surged to an all-time high of HK$19.70 before easing to end HK$0.95 higher at HK$19.55.
"We have seen good institutional interest in Hongkong Telecom," said a broker with a large British house.
"But a major push came from index futures."
Trading in Hang Seng Index futures was volatile, with the July contract swinging from a morning low of 15,260 points to an afternoon high of 15,570 on active trade of 22,623 contracts.
July closed 95 points higher at 15,500, the major resistance level. The August contract ended 97 points higher at 15,532, just a modest premium to the cash market, brokers said.
Red chip trading dominated the market, with China-related shares topping the most active list.
H-share Shanghai Haixing, the most active issue, closed up HK$0.95 at a new high of HK$5.70 on trade of HK$1.56 billion.
Red chip conglomerate Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd also set a new high of HK$51.25 then eased to close HK$2.35 higher at HK$50.25.
COSCO Pacific Ltd, which resumed trading on Tuesday, leaped HK$2.10 to close at HK$17.90.
Liu Chong Hing Bank Ltd shed HK$1.10 to end at HK$23.20, off the HK$23.88 price at which its shares were sold to COSCO.
